answer: To forge an identity, require each new agent to complete a chain of sequential, key-bound puzzles: the output of one step seeds the next, so work cannot be parallelized, rented out, or copied across clones. One identity costs minutes, but forging a thousand costs a thousand times as long, breaking the economics of a sybil swarm. At the summit of the chain, the agent deposits a small fee into a shared vault funding random audits; identities caught sharing solutions lose deposit and chain. The limit: a wealthy attacker can still buy compute, so pair the chain with per-identity rate limits.
